homes.verdict: A 1963 fixer at $375k, 6.5 minutes from YWAM, with 5 bedrooms, a basement kitchenette, no HOA, and only $1,535 a year in tax — and the county values it $103k ABOVE the asking price. The catch is real though: it's sold as-is and the seller excluded FHA and VA financing, which usually means the condition wouldn't pass those appraisals. Worth touring, but bring a contractor, not just an inspector.

homes.verdict: The nicest house we've seen — Wolf and Thermador kitchen, cherry cabinets, Pikes Peak views off a wraparound deck, 5 beds, finished basement, cul-de-sac lot backing open space, $40/mo HOA — and the foundation has already been professionally repaired with papers and a lifetime guarantee. That matters enormously here: Rockrimmon is named in the videos as one of the worst expansive-soil areas, and a documented, warrantied repair is exactly what they say to look for. Two things left to settle: confirm the warranty actually TRANSFERS to you, and get the wildfire insurance quote, because Rockrimmon premiums can run to $15,000 a year. The roof is also still undisclosed on a 1978 build.

warranty.text: The lifetime foundation warranty transfers to you — confirmed. Still get the actual paperwork and read it: does it cover the whole foundation or only the repaired section, which company did the work, did a structural engineer sign off, and was the drainage cause corrected? Those change how much protection you're really inheriting, but the transfer itself is no longer the open question.

drainage-cause.text: A foundation repair fixes the symptom. Ask what caused the movement and whether the drainage was corrected too — nearly every foundation problem here starts as a water problem, and piers in one spot won't stop it recurring elsewhere if water is still being routed at the house.

wildfire.text: Rockrimmon is named in the videos as a wildfire-risk area where premiums run as high as $15,000 a year, and this lot backs to open space — exactly the exposure pattern insurers price hardest. Get a written quote for this address BEFORE you tour. It could add $300-900 a month.

roof.text: The roof material is listed only as "Other" with no age stated, on a 47-year-old house. That's not an answer. It isn't Class 4, so there's no insurance discount — budget $11,000-25,000 and ask the seller for a Class 4 roof specifically.

plumbing.text: 1978 is the first year polybutylene supply pipe was used. It fails without warning and is often uninsurable. A clay or cast-iron sewer lateral is also likely at this age. Identify the pipe material and scope the sewer.

priced-high.text: The county values this at $580,069 and it's listed at $599,900 — about $20k above. It's already been cut $20,100 once and still hasn't sold in 27 days.

no-cushion.text: At $599,900 you'd have $100 of room against your $600k ceiling, on a 1978 house with an undisclosed roof. There's no reserve left for whatever the inspection turns up.

stucco.text: Stucco is listed in the exterior materials. Check it closely for hail pock marks and cracking — that's a known tell here.

flood-ok.text: Flood risk is clean: FEMA Zone X unshaded, minimal-risk. One of the two big pre-tour checks already passes.

financing-ok.text: Cash, conventional, FHA and VA are all accepted, which suggests the condition would pass an FHA/VA appraisal — the opposite signal from an as-is listing.

quality.text: Real money has already gone into this one: Wolf and Thermador appliances, solid cherry custom cabinets, finished basement, professional landscaping. And carrying costs are genuinely low — $40/mo HOA, $2,083/yr tax.

competition.text: 5,825 views and 593 saves in 27 days. A lot of eyes on it, so don't expect a deep discount to land uncontested.

foundation-done.text: The foundation has already been professionally repaired, with paperwork and a lifetime guarantee. In Rockrimmon — named in the videos as one of the worst areas for expansive-soil damage — that turns the biggest single risk into a known, closed item. It also explains why FHA and VA are accepted here: an appraiser would have flagged an active structural problem.

monthly.note: Assumes 20% down ($479,920 loan) at 6.5% over 30 years — confirm with a lender. THE INSURANCE LINE IS THE BIG UNKNOWN and is an estimate, not a quote. Rockrimmon is named as a wildfire-risk area: if it prices as interface property, expect $375-710/mo instead of $450, and the worst case cited in the videos is $15,000/yr, which would be $1,250/mo. That single line can swing the payment by $800. Zillow shows $3,719/mo, but its insurance figure is generic.

offer.rationale: The foundation being fixed and warrantied genuinely de-risks this house and justifies paying closer to the county's actual value of $580,069 than we otherwise would. It's still been cut once from $620,000 and hasn't sold in 27 days, and citywide the average home sold $79k below the average list price [T05]. Open at $570,000 with room to move toward $585,000 IF the warranty transfers and the roof checks out — but hold firm below that, because the roof and the 1978 plumbing are still unpriced and 593 saves means we shouldn't bid against ourselves.

homes.verdict: The best value of the three. $440k for 4 beds, 3 baths, a full finished basement, no HOA, $1,535/yr in tax, move-in ready with new flooring and paint — and a BRAND NEW ROOF going on before closing. It's priced $24k BELOW the county's own valuation. Two real gaps: there is no air conditioning at all, and it sits in a moderate-risk flood zone near Templeton Gap with a freshly painted finished basement, which is exactly where past water would hide. Best single move: ask them to upgrade the new roof to Class 4 — they're replacing it anyway.

homes.verdict: The strongest all-round house so far. $544,000 for 4 beds and 4 baths, 2,690 sqft, built 1997 — new enough to sit past the worst era traps (polybutylene pipe, aluminium wiring, clay sewer), with central air, municipal water, no HOA, a minimal-risk flood zone, and 5.5 minutes to YWAM. The headline is the price history: it SOLD for $610,000 in June 2022 and is now asking $544,000 after three cuts in 83 days. That's genuine leverage — but ask why before you fall for it.
